documents.title: Database platform
documents.plain:
Management uses the control plane. Queries use the data plane. Both address databases by tenant and database identity; clients never select a hosting node.

A tenant owns zero or more databases (0..N). The database is the unit of placement, isolation, backup and lifecycle. One-file-per-tenant is superseded in this proposal; the lanes dataset stays unchanged.

The control plane owns routing logic and the placement registry: (tenant, database) resolves to a hosting VM and epoch. The data plane consults that authority; a cached route is only a hint. Chosen availability policy: fail closed for ALL new admissions when control-plane authority cannot be confirmed. There is no offline lease or heartbeat authorization. Decision issuance is the admission point; no decision prefetch or reuse is permitted. Every request, including an existing session, needs an online one-request admission decision from the authority, bound to database ID, owner epoch/generation, principal, permission, request ID and a deadline of at most 30 seconds. | State / event | Admission / recovery |
| --- | --- |
| Authority reachable, database ACTIVE | Online authorization and current epoch plus durable local ACTIVE state required for each request. |
| Authority unavailable, running agent | Reject new requests, including existing sessions. Already admitted work settles within its deadline; no transfer. |
| MOVING, SUSPENDED, DROPPING or durable local fence | Reject admission even with a previously issued decision. No ownership transfer without confirmed source fencing. |
| Agent restart | Keep closed. Terminate and confirm exit of orphan workers before opening files. Reconcile committed owner/epoch/generation and durable fences online; unavailable authority means stay closed. |
| Controller crash after placement commit, before activation ACK | Target remains sole committed owner; it stays closed until idempotent activation reconciles that commit. Source stays fenced. Never roll back to stale ownership. |

documents.title: Suspend, resume, backup and restore
documents.plain:
Suspend uses the same per-database gate and drain as move; SUSPENDED blocks opens and existing-session admissions. Resume requires verified file readiness, ACTIVE state and a fresh epoch. Backup takes a consistent per-database SQLite backup with an identity/generation manifest and verification; it does not copy a live main file alone. Restore stages and verifies a backup before a fenced, drained generation swap and fresh-epoch activation. IDs/authorization must still match; restoring data cannot resurrect deleted grants. Operations use durable IDs and state transitions, never a distributed transaction across SQL and files. This design chooses temporary unavailability and reconciliation over unproven online relocation or failover.

documents.title: VM agent: private execution and deadlines
documents.plain:
Every hosting VM runs a daemon labelled VM agent (process), software, not AI. It is the sole last-mile tenant-file access boundary on that VM. Outside services never access its disk. Its private managed statement-lane workers execute only behind this agent boundary; they expose no independent file or RPC authority. On instruction the agent executes queries and returns results, provisions, opens/closes, suspends/resumes, snapshots/backs up, copies out/receives moves, restores and deletes files, and reports health, size and usage to the control plane. Retain the lanes proposal bounded pool, scheduler and handle-cache policies, keyed by database with aggregate tenant and VM ceilings. Bound queue count and bytes, concurrent reads, one writer per database, open handles and lane count. Reject or backpressure excess admission; fairly schedule databases within tenant budgets so many databases cannot consume the VM. Evict idle handles only after transactions settle. Require disk plus WAL/snapshot headroom and bounded backup/move I/O reservations; throttle or reject when exhausted. Reserve supervisor/control capacity for fencing and cancellation under execution saturation. Quotas are accounting, not a tenant-wide execution lock. 0..N is cardinality, not unlimited capacity. Logical/file isolation is provided; VM/process failure and resource contention remain shared. Numeric limits and fairness weights remain OPEN configuration choices.
